constitutive_assumptions: Uniform hydraulic pressure distribution against the inner wall of the elastic tube
Constant material volume of the elastic tube during deformation
Negligible circumferential deformation of the outer wall of the elastic tube due to constraints of the fabric layers and stitches
Bending actuator finger modeled as a bending cylindrical beam in both undeformed and deformed conditions
Negligible friction between the wrinkled fabric and the elastic tube during expansion
Wrinkled fabric bending stiffness is considered negligible compared to that of the elastic tube
Neutral axis located at the non-stretchable fabric layer
External loads applied to the gripper are not included in the analytical bending angle model
control_variables: Gripper finger thickness with VSF and gecko adhesive (9 mm)
Elastic latex rubber tube dimensions (inner diameter 3.175 mm, outer diameter 4.7625 mm)
PET tube dimensions (inner diameter 0.89 mm, outer diameter 2.16 mm, length 140 mm)
Fabric conduit width for VSF (6 mm)
Hydraulic pressure during holding force evaluation (600 kPa)
Pulling distance in holding force tests (20 mm)
Heating temperature upper threshold (80 °C) and cooling endpoint (50 °C)
Sensor cyclic test actuation frequency (0.2 Hz for 200 cycles)
Volume fraction of carbon black in conductive mixture (10% carbon black in EGaIn/carbon grease)
dependent_variables: Heating time and ambient cooling time (seconds)
VSF and gecko adhesive surface temperature (°C)
Peak holding force in vertical/gripping configuration (N)
Peak holding force in horizontal/pull-out configuration (N)
Relative change in sensor electrical resistance (delta R / R0)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A sheet-shaped fabric bending actuator fabricated using textile techniques (sewing and tube routing) enables edge/surface contact and planar integration of additional components, overcoming point-contact instability of fusiform actuators.
Directional wedge-shaped gecko microstructures molded from Sylgard 170 on wax molds enhance surface holding force via van der Waals adhesion.

A thermo-responsive variable stiffness filament (VSF) comprising a PET tube and internal heating coil achieves a ~26-fold bending stiffness variation (0.057 to 1.484 N/mm) between rigid and soft states.
The tubular geometry of the VSF reduces thermal mass, enabling an ambient cooling time of 25 s alone and 31 s with gecko adhesive to transition from 80 °C to 50 °C.
A simple analytical beam-bending model under quasi-hydrostatic and volume-invariance assumptions predicts finger bending angles up to 197.6° at 550 kPa.
Integrating VSF and gecko adhesive increases peak holding force by up to 655% in the gripping mode and 507% in the pull-out mode for a 24 mm cylindrical object.
The two-fingered gripper (3.7 g per finger) lifted payloads up to 1.1 kg, achieving a payload-to-weight ratio of 148.6 times.

A stencil-printed conductive composite of EGaIn liquid metal and carbon grease provides bending strain feedback over 200 cycles with minimal drift (-1.79% expanding, -0.01% closing) without thermal interference from the VSF.

experimental_setup: Syringe pump controlled by a DC-motor-powered translational stage (0 to 60 mm displacement in 10 mm increments) to apply hydraulic pressure
Honeywell 40PC250G2A pressure sensor connected to transmission tubes for fluid pressure measurement
Nikon digital camera for recording bending deformation and extracting angular displacement
Mark-10 force gauge paired with a fixed plastic blocking frame to measure actuator tip blocked force under pressurization and depressurization
Cantilever deflection setup to quantify bending stiffness changes of the VSF in rigid and soft states
Thermal characterization setup using variable DC power supplies (0.1 A to 0.5 A), FLIR thermal imaging camera, and Nikon DSLR camera to record heating and cooling curves

Holding force test rig using 3D-printed cylindrical test bars (24 mm and 28 mm diameter), inextensible string, translation stage pulling 20 mm, Mark-10 force gauge, Quanser QPIDe DAQ, and MATLAB/Simulink

Sensor characterization bench consisting of a Zaber translational stage (X-LRQ150L-E) actuating the gripper for 200 cycles at 0.2 Hz, a 4-wire voltage divider readout circuit, Quanser QPIDe, and Simulink
Object grasping demonstrations manipulating fragile, slippery, and heavy objects (tomatoes, eggs, chocolate egg, kiwi, cucumber, 200 g metal weight, 1.1 kg tool case)
future_work: Employ alternative PCMs such as shape memory polymers (SMPs) with lower transition temperatures to enhance safety and cycle speed
Measure and characterize the continuous stiffness response of the VSF across multiple intermediate temperatures rather than only at rigid and soft states
Develop an active cooling system utilizing the hollow tubular lumen of the VSF for cold air circulation to shorten cooling duration
Embed miniature temperature sensors directly into the VSF and apply closed-loop thermal control to avoid temperature overshoot
Develop and integrate nonlinear hysteresis models to better capture actuator behavior
Incorporate soft tactile/force sensors (capacitive or resistive) for real-time contact force feedback and object size estimation
Implement a closed-loop nonlinear control scheme based on multi-sensor feedback
Optimize the conductive composite strain sensor to reduce hysteresis and improve sensing accuracy
independent_variables: Electrical current supplied to the VSF heating coil (0.1 A, 0.2 A, 0.3 A, 0.4 A, 0.5 A)
Gripper hardware configuration (pure fabric gripper, with VSF, with gecko adhesive, with VSF + gecko adhesive)
Pulling configuration / test orientation (gripping/vertical pulling vs. pull-out/horizontal pulling)
Object cylinder diameter (24 mm vs. 28 mm)
Object mass and surface properties in manipulation tests
Number of mechanical actuation cycles (up to 200 cycles)
limitations_inferred: Manual assembly steps (wrinkle manual rearrangement, knot tying with thread and superglue, manual rod threading) pose challenges for uniform mass manufacturing despite claims of apparel-engineering scalability
An ambient cooling duration of 31 seconds remains comparatively slow for high-cycle-rate industrial pick-and-place applications
Holding force experiments were limited to smooth cylindrical bars, leaving performance under abrasive, dusty, or irregularly contoured contacts unquantified
Gecko microstructures and silicone coatings may be susceptible to contamination and wear-induced loss of adhesion over extended use cycles
Hydraulic operation necessitates pumps, valves, and fluid management that may introduce system bulk and leakage risks in field deployments
limitations_stated_by_authors: Nonlinearity of elastic materials causes pronounced hysteresis between pressurization and depressurization phases, which the analytical model does not account for
The analytical bending model neglects external loads applied to the gripper during interaction
Manual fabrication introduces inevitable inconsistencies and pressure fluctuations during dynamic operation, leading to slight deviations between analytical predictions and experiments
PET tubes require a relatively high transition temperature (~67 °C glass transition, heated to 80 °C), increasing energy usage, cycle time, and safety risks for nearby human operators
Stiffness of the VSF was evaluated only at two discrete temperature points (rigid and soft states) rather than across a continuous range
Adding the gecko adhesive layer creates a thermal barrier that slows the cooling rate of the VSF from 25 s to 31 s
Manual shutoff of electric current at 80 °C resulted in thermal overshoot
Holding force enhancement in the pull-out configuration is significantly lower than in the gripping configuration because it relies purely on shear/surface friction
Carbon grease within the conductive ink introduces small hysteresis into the strain sensor response during cycling
Holding force with VSF diminishes on larger objects (28 mm cylinder) that cannot be completely wrapped by the gripper fingers
main_results: Successfully engineered a sheet-like, fluid-driven soft fabric bending actuator and two-fingered gripper using scalable apparel sewing techniques, mitigating transverse instability and point-contact issues
Demonstrated that integrating a PET-based VSF and gecko adhesive boosts peak holding force by up to 655% (to 8.212 N) in gripping mode and 507% (to 2.293 N) in pull-out mode for a 24 mm cylinder
Achieved a relatively rapid ambient cooling time of 31 s (51 s full cycle) for the VSF due to the lower thermal mass of its hollow tubular structure relative to solid phase-change systems
Formulated a volume-conserving, beam-based analytical model that reliably predicts the nonlinear relationship between input hydraulic pressure and bending angle up to 197.6° at 550 kPa

Formulated a stencil-printed liquid metal/carbon grease conductive composite sensor on fabric that tracked bending deformation over 200 cycles with low drift (-1.79% expanding, -0.01% closing) and demonstrated thermal isolation from the heating element
Demonstrated robust grasping of delicate items (ripe tomatoes, chocolate eggs) as well as heavy loads up to 1.1 kg (payload-to-weight ratio of 148.6 times relative to finger mass)
modeling_methods: Analytical model representing the bending finger as a bending cylindrical beam under quasi-hydrostatic conditions
Volumetric invariance condition applied to the elastic tube during stretching and hydraulic pressurization phases
Static force balance equating internal hydraulic driving force and axial elastic tube restoring force to determine stretch ratio
Moment equilibrium between external moment induced by asymmetric axial extension and internal elastic bending moment
Young's modulus calculation derived from Shore A hardness of the elastomer using an empirical formulation from literature
Parallel axis theorem used to calculate the second moment of area of the composite bending cross-section relative to the neutral axis
performance_metrics: Maximum finger bending angle: 197.6° (± 3.5°) at 550 kPa hydraulic pressure
Bending stiffness variation of VSF: approximately 26 times (~2500% increase, 0.057 to 1.484 N/mm) between soft and rigid states
VSF heating time: ~15 s at 0.5 A and ~20 s at 0.4 A to heat from 25 °C to 80 °C
VSF cooling time: ~25 s for bare VSF and ~31 s for VSF with gecko adhesive (ambient cooling from 80 °C to 50 °C)
Total thermal cycle time: ~45 s (VSF alone) and ~51 s (VSF with gecko adhesive)
Holding force (gripping configuration, 24 mm cylinder): 8.212 N (655% increase over bare gripper)
Holding force (gripping configuration, 28 mm cylinder): 4.931 N (562% increase over bare gripper)
Holding force (pull-out configuration, 24 mm cylinder): 2.293 N (507% increase over bare gripper)
Holding force (pull-out configuration, 28 mm cylinder): 2.032 N (395% increase over bare gripper)
Maximum payload capacity: 1.1 kg tool case (gripping) and 200 g metal weight (pull-out)
Payload-to-weight ratio: 148.6 times (based on 3.7 g per finger, 7.4 g total gripper finger mass)
Strain sensor drift error after 200 cycles: -1.79% (expansion) and -0.01% (closure)
possible_gap_implications: Employing thin-walled, hollow tubular phase-change geometries within textile soft actuators could bridge the trade-off between high load-bearing capacity and slow thermal switching times in variable-stiffness soft robotics

Coupling directional dry gecko adhesives with controllable stiffness elements suggests an approach to independently modulate normal wrapping rigidity and tangential shear traction for grasping fragile or low-friction items

Planar, sheet-like fabric architectures provide a viable substrate for co-locating stretchable sensors, phase-change stiffeners, and fluidic bladders without relying on complex multi-material casting molds
paper.research_objective: To develop and characterize a facile and scalable soft robotic fabric gripper fabricated via apparel engineering, featuring sheet-shaped hydraulic bending actuators integrated with a thermo-responsive variable stiffness filament, gecko-inspired dry adhesives, and a liquid-metal/carbon-particle fabric strain sensor to achieve conformable grasping, high load capacity, and bending state monitoring.
paper.research_problem: Conventional fluid-driven soft grippers have low stiffness due to their constituent soft materials, resulting in poor load capacity in high-load applications; furthermore, conventional fabrication via silicone elastomer molding is difficult to scale, and common fusiform-shaped fabric actuators suffer from point contact, lateral instability, and difficulty in integrating functional components such as sensors or variable-stiffness elements.
paper.title: Soft robotic fabric gripper with gecko adhesion and variable stiffness
